items.title: Section: How Form and Mind Mutually Support Each Other Among the Faculties

items.zh: 問：幾於非色助伴義轉？答：七色根。問：幾色非色為助伴耶？答：餘有義根。問：五色根何義？答：色等五各別境。
items.en: Question: how many operate as a companion enabling non-form faculties? Answer: the seven form faculties. Question: how many non-form faculties serve as a companion to the form faculties? Answer: the remaining faculties possessing objective meaning. Question: what is the meaning of the five form faculties? Answer: colour and the rest are each their own separate object.

items.title: Section: Twelve Faculties, Twelve Objects — From Ordinary Perception to the Threshold of Nirvāṇa

items.zh: 問：第六根何義？答：一切法。問：男女根何義？答：因欲相應，即觸所攝。問：五受根何義？答：隨順苦、樂、憂、喜、捨處，即六根義。問：信根何義？答：應得應捨所有境界。問：精進根何義？答：即於二種若得、若捨俱無所憚。問：念根何義？答：於聞思修憶持不忘。問：定根何義？答：奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。問：慧根何義？答：所知真實。問：未知欲知根何義？答：修諦現觀者，從善法欲已去，於一切方便道中，即彼五根義當知是此義。問：已知根何義？答：從預流果乃至金剛喻定，即彼五根義當知是此義。問：具知根何義？答：從初無學道乃至無餘涅槃界，即彼五根義當知是此義。
items.en: Question: what is the object of the mind faculty? Answer: all phenomena. Question: of the male and female faculties? Answer: whatever is associated with desire, subsumed under touch. Question: of the five feeling faculties? Answer: whatever accords with pain, pleasure, sorrow, joy, and equanimity — the object of the six faculties. Question: of the faith faculty? Answer: whatever should be attained or relinquished. Question: of the diligence faculty? Answer: pursuing that same attaining and relinquishing without hesitation. Question: of the mindfulness faculty? Answer: what has been heard, reflected upon, and cultivated, retained without forgetting. Question: of the concentration faculty? Answer: calm-abiding and insight. Question: of the wisdom faculty? Answer: reality as genuinely known. Question: of the aspirant's faculty? Answer: for one cultivating direct realisation of the truths, everything from the arising of wholesome aspiration onward throughout the entire preparatory path — this should be understood as the very object of those five faculties. Question: of the knower's faculty? Answer: from the fruit of stream-entry to the vajra-like concentration — this should be understood as that same object. Question: of the faculty of complete knowledge? Answer: from the first stage beyond training to the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder — this should be understood as that same object.

items.title: Section: Seven and Fourteen and One — Sorting the Faculties by Form, Visibility, and Resistance

items.zh: 問：幾有色，有色為義？答：七。問：幾無色，有色無色為義？答：除命根，餘一切。問：幾非有色非無色，非有色非無色為義？答：即此命根，是假法故。問：幾有見，有見為義？答：一切非有見。一有色以有見為義；及餘非有色一分。
items.en: Question: how many possess form, and take form as their object? Answer: seven. Question: how many are formless, and take both form and the formless as their object? Answer: all except the life faculty. Question: how many are neither form nor formless, and take neither as their object? Answer: the life faculty alone, being a provisional phenomenon. Question: how many are visible, and take the visible as their object? Answer: in the ultimate sense, none. One that possesses form takes the visible as its object, together with a portion of the remaining formless faculties.

items.title: Section: Why Pain and Sorrow Break the Usual Pattern of Defiled and Undefiled

items.zh: 問：幾有對，有對為義？答：七有色及餘無色無對一分。問：幾有漏，有漏為義？答：唯七。除最後二及苦、憂根，餘有漏、無漏，以有漏、無漏為義。當知苦根有漏、無漏，以有漏為義。憂根有漏，以有漏、無漏為義。
items.en: Question: how many possess resistance, and take resistance as their object? Answer: the seven form faculties, together with a portion of the remaining formless, non-resistant faculties. Question: how many are defiled, and take the defiled as their object? Answer: only seven. Excepting the final two and the pain and sorrow faculties, the remaining faculties are both defiled and undefiled, taking both as their object. It should be understood that the pain faculty is both defiled and undefiled, but takes only the defiled as its object. The sorrow faculty is defiled, but takes both the defiled and undefiled as its object.

items.zh: 未知欲知根，若遠沙門果，世間行所攝，是有漏；若近沙門果，出世行所攝，是無漏。

items.title: Section: A Faculty That Has Already Passed Can Still Take the Present as Its Object

items.zh: 問：幾有為，有為為義？答：一切是有為。八有為為義，餘有為、無為為義。問：幾有諍，有諍為義？答：如說有漏，當知此亦爾。如說有諍，當知有愛味、依耽嗜、世間、出世間等亦爾。問：幾過去，過去為義？答：除有色根及苦根，餘有義一分。若有色根及苦根在過去，非過去為義。問：幾過去，現在為義？答：即如所說一分。當知即此在過去，以未來為義。又即此在現在，以過去、未來為義。
items.en: Question: how many are conditioned, and take the conditioned as their object? Answer: all are conditioned; eight take only the conditioned as their object, the rest take both the conditioned and unconditioned. As with defilement, so too should contentiousness, attachment to taste, habitual indulgence, and mundane versus transcendent status be understood. Question: how many belong to the past, and take the past as their object? Answer: excepting the physical faculties and the pain faculty, a portion of the remaining faculties belonging to the past do so. The physical faculties and the pain faculty, though they too belong to the past once ceased, do not take the past as their object.

items.title: Section: Present Senses, Timeless Mind, and the Seven Ways a Faculty Belongs to a Realm

items.zh: 問：幾現在，現在為義？答：一切有色根及苦根，并前所說一分。又此一分在未來，以過去、未來、現在為義。若諸色根在未來，非未來為義。苦根亦爾。問：幾欲界繫，欲界繫為義？答：四。二，欲、色界繫，欲界繫為義。三，欲、色界繫，欲、色界繫為義。二，欲、色界繫及不繫，欲、色、無色界繫及不繫為義。七，欲、色、無色界繫及不繫，彼義亦爾。一，色界繫及不繫，一切繫不繫為義。二，不繫，一切繫不繫為義。
items.en: Question: how many belong to the present and take the present as their object? Answer: all the physical faculties and the pain faculty, together with the portion already described. This same portion, when located in the future, takes the past, future, and present as its object. The physical faculties, when located in the future, do not take the future as their object; the pain faculty likewise. Question: how many are confined to the desire realm and take the desire realm as their object? Answer: four. Two are confined to the desire and form realms and take the desire realm as their object. Three are confined to the desire and form realms and take both as their object. Two are confined to the desire realm, the form realm, and the unbound state, and take all three realms and the unbound state as their object. Seven are confined to all three realms and the unbound state, and take that same range as their object. One is confined to the form realm and the unbound state, yet takes the entire range as its object. Two are confined only to the unbound state, yet likewise take the entire range as their object.

items.title: Section: Faculties That Are Only Ever Wholesome, and Faculties That Can Be Any of the Three

items.zh: 問：幾善，善為義？答：八，唯善，善、不善、無記為義。五，善、不善、無記，善、不善、無記為義。
items.en: Question: how many are wholesome, and take the wholesome as their object? Answer: eight are purely wholesome, yet take the wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral as their object. Five are wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral in their own nature, and likewise take the wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral as their object.

items.title: Section: Closing Moral Quality, and Sorting the Faculties by Trainee, Adept, and Neither

items.zh: 一，善、不善，善、不善、無記為義。五，無記，無記為義。二，無記，善、不善、無記為義。問：幾學，學為義？如是等。答：九，學、無學、非學非無學，以三種為義。七，非學非無學，即以此為義。一，通三種，非學非無學為義。一，學、非學非無學，以三種為義。二，學，以三種為義。一，無學，以三種為義。
items.en: One is wholesome and unwholesome, and takes the wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral as its object. Five are neutral, and take the neutral as their object. Two are neutral, and take the wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral as their object. Question: how many belong to trainees, and take the trainee's state as their object? Answer: nine belong to trainees, those beyond training, and neither, and take all three as their object. Seven belong to neither, and take only that as their object. One spans all three, yet takes only "neither" as its object. One belongs to trainees and to neither, and takes all three as its object. Two belong to trainees, and take all three as their object. One belongs to those beyond training, and takes all three as its object.

items.title: Section: What Must Be Severed by Insight, What by Sustained Practice, and What Needs No Severing At All

items.zh: 問：幾見所斷，見所斷為義？如是等。答：十四，一分見所斷，一分修所斷。十二，一分修所斷，一分非所斷。謂即十四中六及餘六。餘二非所斷。此中有色諸根，見、修所斷為義；無色諸根，三種為義，謂見、修所斷，非所斷義。
items.en: Question: how many are to be severed by the path of vision, and take that as their object? Answer: fourteen are partly to be severed by vision and partly by cultivation. Twelve are partly to be severed by cultivation and partly not to be severed at all — namely six of the fourteen just named, together with six others. The remaining two are not to be severed at all. Among these, faculties possessing form take only vision and cultivation as their object; formless faculties take all three — vision, cultivation, and no severing at all — as their object.

blocks.text: A dense day of classification. Read it as a set of questions asked of each faculty: what does it take as object, is it good or bad, which realm, and when is it cut?

subs.head: Form and mind support each other

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seven physical faculties act at the same time as mental phenomena; they are "companions", not associated in the strict sense.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the object of the male and female faculties falls under touch. The wisdom faculty penetrates the reality of things, the ultimate truth.
The eye is the one faculty that "has sight": it is form, and the chief cause of seeing.
Pain can be contaminated or not; sorrow is contaminated. Master Cháng Bǎi: an arhat no longer clings, yet bodily pain still arises.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the physical faculties take only present objects; the mental ones can take the three times.
Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm gods have nose and tongue but do not use them.
Eight faculties are purely wholesome yet can take all three moral natures as object. Sorrow over not yet reaching nirvāṇa belongs to learners and ordinary beings.
Master Cháng Bǎi: faculties of the lower realms are cut at the path of seeing, since after that one no longer falls.
"Sorrow over not yet reaching nirvāṇa" is counted as wholesome. Not all sorrow is an obstacle.

quiz.q: The English has "operate as a companion enabling non-form faculties." Is "enabling" fitting?
options: companion here is coexistence, acting together, with no one enabling another; "enabling" is an addition
fitting: physical faculties are the sole cause of the non-form, none existing without them, the formless realm included
unfitting: it should be "opposing"
unfitting: the Chinese has no 助伴
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: companion here means the seven physical faculties coexist with non-form phenomena, not the mutual association of mind and factors; they act at the same time with mental phenomena, and this is called companion. So there is no directional enabling. The English adds a causal relation the Chinese does not state.

quiz.q: What are the objects of the male and female, faith, and diligence faculties?
options: male and female: all phenomena; faith: calm and insight; diligence: retention, as the lecture matches them
all three take nirvāṇa
male and female: what joins with desire, under touch; faith: what should be attained or relinquished; diligence: both, without hesitation
none has an object
quiz.why: The treatise gives these objects. Master Cháng Bǎi: the object of the male and female faculties rests on the contact of the body faculty, and so it is subsumed under touch. Faith concerns what should be attained or relinquished, and diligence pursues both without hesitation. In the English 義 here is "object."

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain wisdom's object and those of the three uncontaminated faculties?
options: wisdom knows only worldly learning; the three's objects differ wholly from the five's, one being contaminated
wisdom's object is form
wisdom penetrates ultimate reality; faith and the others' objects are those of the aspirant's faculty, differing only in strength
the three have no object
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the wisdom faculty penetrates the reality of phenomena, the ultimate truth; this is reality as known. The objects of faith and the rest are the same as those of the aspirant's faculty; the knower and the aspirant differ only in strength. The English "reality as genuinely known" reads 所知 as an act rather than an object.

quiz.q: The English has "how many are visible" for 幾有見. How does the Sub-commentary read this?
options: it asks how many can be seen, all five being visible, so the English is exact, as the Sub-commentary says
it asks about views, meaning wrong views
it asks how many faculties can see; the eye itself is not visible; "visible" reverses the direction
it asks about the divine eye
quiz.why: The Sub-commentary says the question is how many faculties can see, called having sight. Master Cháng Bǎi: the eye is called the one possessing form, itself being form, and it is the chief condition for seeing, and so one conventionally says the eye sees. The English "visible" asks what can be seen, which reverses the direction of the question.

quiz.q: How do the pain and sorrow faculties stand regarding contamination and object?
options: pain is both, taking the contaminated as object; sorrow is contaminated, taking both as object
pain is contaminated, taking both; sorrow is both, taking the contaminated, since it reaches the path
both are uncontaminated
both are contaminated, taking only the contaminated
quiz.why: The treatise says pain is contaminated and uncontaminated, taking the contaminated as object; sorrow is contaminated, taking both as object. Master Cháng Bǎi: an arhat no longer clings to the aggregates as self, so an arhat's pain can be called uncontaminated; and taking the noble path as object, one feels sorrow joined with renunciation.

quiz.q: Why do the physical faculties and pain not take the past as object, and what of the rest?
options: the physical can take past and future, the eye seeing past things; the non-form take only the present
all faculties take only the present
all faculties take only the past
they take only the present; the thirteen non-form faculties are mental and can take all three times
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seven physical faculties and the bodily faculty of pain take only present objects, and so are excepted; the thirteen non-form faculties are mind and factors, able to take the three times. This agrees with the earlier teaching that the five sense-consciousnesses take the present.

quiz.q: What do the non-form faculties such as mind take in the three times?
options: in each time only that time, unable to reach others, just like physical faculties
only the future
wherever located in the three times, they can take past, present, and future
none can take anything
quiz.why: The treatise says this portion, located in the future, takes past, future, and present as object. Master Cháng Bǎi: non-form faculties such as mind can take the three times in any of the three; the point to stress is that the seven physical faculties take only the present, while the mind faculty has all three as its domain.

quiz.q: Which two are of the desire and form realms yet take the desire realm as object, and why?
options: eye and ear; form-realm gods do not use them, unlike nose and tongue, which work there
nose and tongue; form-realm gods have them but do not use them, smell and taste being only of the desire realm
male and female; the form realm has sexes
pain and sorrow; the form realm has them
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: form-realm gods do have nose and tongue faculties, but they do not use them. So these two are bound to desire and form yet take only the desire realm as object. So 有鼻舌根 does not mean they function there.

quiz.q: The English has "defiled" for both 有漏 and 染汙. What is the problem?
options: the seven are contaminated yet neutral, so "defiled" conflicts with neutral; 有漏 differs from 染汙 and should be "contaminated"
no problem: 有漏 means defiled, physical faculties being evil, so "defiled" is exact and does not conflict
both should be "impure"
both should be "mental"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: all ripened results are neutral, including the five faculties, the male and female faculties, and the life faculty. So the physical faculties are contaminated yet not defiled. The English uses "defiled" for 有漏 here and for 染汙 elsewhere, which would make a neutral faculty defiled. "Contaminated" would keep the two apart.

quiz.q: Which are the eight purely wholesome faculties and the five of all three natures?
options: the eight are the seven physical with life; the five are faith and the rest, which may join affliction and so are of all three natures
the eight are faith and the rest with the three uncontaminated; the five are pain, pleasure, joy, equanimity, and mind
the eight are mind with the seven physical; the five are the five feelings
the eight are the five with sorrow, pain, joy; the five are the sense faculties
quiz.why: The treatise separates nature from object: eight are purely wholesome yet take all three natures as object. Master Cháng Bǎi: these eight belong only to the wholesome but have the three natures as object; pain, pleasure, joy, equanimity, and mind extend to all three natures and also have them as object.

quiz.q: Which is the one belonging to trainees and to neither, and why, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: pain: bodily pain reaches trainees, adepts, and ordinary beings, since even arhats feel pain, and so three
the knower's faculty: only trainees have it
sorrow: worry about not attaining nirvāṇa, extending to trainees and ordinary beings, with all three as object
complete knowledge: only adepts have it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: worrying about not attaining nirvāṇa, sorrow extends to trainees and ordinary beings and has all three as object. Pain is the separate case in the same section: it spans all three persons but takes only "neither" as object. The English "spans all three" reflects this.

quiz.q: Why are physical faculties divided into those severed by vision and by cultivation?
options: evil-destiny faculties are severed at vision, after which one does not fall; human and divine ones finish only at nirvāṇa without remainder
physical faculties are afflictions, all severed at vision, and so arhats have no body
vision severs the eye, cultivation the rest
vision severs good-destiny faculties, cultivation evil-destiny ones
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: faculties of evil destinies are severed at the path of vision, since after that one no longer falls; the path of cultivation is complete only on entering nirvāṇa without remainder, so even faculties of human and divine destinies are to be severed. Severing here concerns destinies, not the body as such.
